blockers: All idle-sheet frames appear pixel-identical for Celina, Agnes, and Gambler. There is no readable animation, anticipation, settle, breathing, cloth motion, hat motion, or character-specific timing.
Agnes visibly floats: the two block feet are detached from the lower body with large gaps and do not establish convincing weight or ground contact.
Locomotion is not evaluable from the supplied sheets; no walk-cycle poses, contact frames, passing poses, or body counter-motion are present.
The characters use blank, featureless faces and highly simplified primitive construction, leaving Celina and Agnes especially close to generic mannequin silhouettes at game scale.
high_value_changes: Build actual idle cycles with at least 6-8 meaningful poses per character: subtle torso/breathing offsets, head settling, limb drift, and a clear return-to-anchor frame rather than duplicated cells.
Fix Agnes's feet-to-body connection. Add a readable lower-leg/ankle transition, align both feet to a shared ground plane, and use compression on the downbeat to sell weight.

Create distinct motion signatures: Celina's robe and staff should sway minimally with controlled vertical breathing; Agnes should have a heavier, wider torso settle; Gambler should use a jaunty off-axis balance with hat, sleeve, and raised-hand follow-through.

Add one or two high-contrast identity cues at native scale, especially for Celina and Agnes. Current clothing blocks and blank faces do most of the work, which makes recognition fragile outside the lineup.
Author locomotion as a real contact-driven cycle. Keep a stable pelvis/head anchor, place feet deliberately on contact and passing frames, and avoid translating the whole sprite uniformly.
optional_notes: Gambler has the strongest immediate silhouette because of the triangular hat, raised arm, satchel, and diagonal leg, but the single bent leg reads more like a static kick than grounded locomotion.
Celina's staff is a useful identity prop, but it extends below the robe and can read as an accidental trailing pixel/anchor artifact at native scale.
The palette is coherent and sufficiently separated across the three characters; additional texture is not needed. Prioritize motion and construction over surface detail.
strongest_improvements: The three characters are clearly separated by broad silhouette families: hooded robe, squared heavy body, and angular hat with asymmetric pose.
Gambler's silhouette and purple/green palette provide the clearest character-specific read.
The lineup maintains consistent rendering treatment, dark background contrast, and broadly coherent scale.
single_most_important_next_change: Replace the duplicated idle-sheet cells with genuine, anchored animation cycles that include visible anticipation, weighty settle, and character-specific secondary motion; do not proceed to polish until frame-to-frame change is readable at native 192px game scale.
